articleTitle: Using long-range temporal correlations in the brain to predict intellectual development in children
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this study, we employed electroencephalographic recordings to predict intelligence quotient (IQ) in children aged 8 to 10 years. The intelligence quotient (IQ) was measured using Raven’s progressive matrices. The detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) method was employed to quantify the autocorrelations of the signal. The results demonstrated that the exponent of DFA in the frontal brain area in the alpha frequency range is correlated with IQ. Consequently, DFA provides supplementary data regarding IQ-related cognitive functions and can be employed as a means of objective assessment of a child’s intelligence.

articleTitle: FIRI-2018: MATLAB package for the lower ionosphere model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: It is important to have information about the electron density in the lower ionosphere for predicting the energy parameters of very low frequency radio links. It can be provided by the Faraday International Reference Ionosphere model. We have implemented this model in the MATLAB programming software as a set of scripts, functions and data files. Since the wave method for predicting the electric field strength on the radio path is sensitive to low electron densities at low altitudes, the developed package implements exponential extrapolation of the electron density for altitudes below 55 km. The MATLAB source code is available at Github and MATLAB Central resources.

articleTitle: Different types of multistability in the Chialvo map
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We study different types of multistability in the neuron model with discrete time - the Chialvo map. Multistability of the first type corresponds to the case when resonant and non-resonant invariant curve coexist in phase space. For another parameters of the model we have found coexistence between invariant curve and chaos. We analyze mechanisms of appearance and destruction of multistability.

articleTitle: Immunological correlates of ischemic stroke severity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between cytokines and ischemic stroke severity to discover biomarkers that can be used as predictors of functional outcome of patient rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Neuropunk revolution: energy consumption aspects of modern AI
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, we present the comparison of modern ANNs and SNNs indicating several orders of magnitude differences. As well as optimisation approaches for the SNNs starting from bio-plausible models implemented as SNNs till memristive schematics still implementing neurobiological phenomena.

articleTitle: Advanced Modeling for Adaptive DBS: Capturing Parkinson’s Disease Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Parkinson’s Disease (PD) represents a significant challenge due to its complex symptomatology and the diminishing efficacy of pharmacological treatments over time. Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a viable alternative, particularly through its adaptive variant (aDBS), which aims to modulate neural activity via feedback-controlled stimulation. However, the development of aDBS is hindered by oversimplified disease models that fail to capture the nuanced dynamics of the disease observed in patients. This paper addresses the need for more realistic PD models that integrate comprehensive physiological and neural dynamics to enhance aDBS training and efficacy. We present a conceptual framework based on the Kuramoto model, enriched with modifications to incorporate spatial, temporal, and frequency characteristics of PD-related neural activity. Spatial features include localized stimulation and recording capabilities reflective of advanced electrode technologies. Temporarily, the model accounts for the highly variable and stochastic nature of neural activity, essential for realistic simulations of neural behavior. Frequency aspects are detailed to match the neuro-biologically observed spectra in PD patients, focusing on the beta frequency band’s role in symptom manifestation. Through integrating these dimensions into a cohesive model, we aim to refine aDBS approaches and improve their clinical outcomes by providing a more realistic simulation environment for algorithm development and testing. This work lays the groundwork for future research on the intersection of neuroengineering and clinical neuroscience, promising to advance the adaptability and precision of therapeutic interventions for PD and potentially other neurological conditions.

articleTitle: Synthesis and size effect on resistive switching in ZnO:Ga thin films for neuromorphic applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper shows the results of investigation of the influence of synthesis modes of ZnO:Ga thin films by pulsed laser deposition on their morphological and electrophysical characteristics. Experimental studies of the influence of dimensional effects on the resistive switching parameters of memristor structures based on doped ZnO thin films have been carried out. The relationship between the morphological parameters of the films, their thickness and resistive switching characteristics has been established. The results showing how the thickness, surface roughness and average grain diameter influence the ratio of resistances in the high-resistance and low-resistance states, as well as the switching voltage $\mathbf{U}_{\text {set }}$ and $\mathbf{U}_{\text {res }}$ have been obtained.

articleTitle: AI methods of control for distributed space systems: a review
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper is a short review of the problems arising in control of distributed systems of spacecraft due to different kinds of uncertainties and of various AI-based approaches to deal with them. The considered uncertainties are caused by external and internal disturbances of different nature. The methods to deal with the uncertainties include neural networks, fuzzy logic, evolutionary algorithms, randomized algorithms and reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: Topological markers of dynamical regimes in spiking neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Understanding the complex dynamics of neural networks is crucial for unraveling the mechanisms underlying brain functioning. In this study, we approach the issue of synchrony in the collective behavior of neurons from a topological perspective, employing the machinery of principal component analysis (PCA), persistent homology (PH), and the embedding dimension. Using the Morris-Lecar neural model as an example, we demonstrate how these instruments can be applied to the data of activity of a spiking neural network to characterize its dynamic regime. We show that topological data analysis (TDA) of neural activity can serve as an effective mean of neurodynamic inquiry and provide new insights into the function of neural networks. Thereby, this work motivates further research on the application of topological methods to the problems of neural dynamics.

articleTitle: Ensemble methods for representation of fMRI, EEG/MEG data in graph form for classification of brain states
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The goal of this work is to propose a method for representing functional magnetic resonance imaging data and electroencephalography/magnetoencephalography data in the form of graphs reflecting the interactions of brain regions for brain state classification tasks. This method is based on ensemble learning to improve generalizability, accuracy, robustness and parallelism of the classification model, which is important when analyzing such large, complexly structured and noisy data as neuroimaging data.

articleTitle: Towards modeling local sleep phenomena: a toy model of a smallest sleep unit
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Recent research in sleep physiology demonstrates that sleep state does not necessarily involve the entire brain. To explain these new findings, the concept of “local sleep” has been proposed. This research focuses on mathematical modeling of minimal “sleep unit”. The proposed model shows transition to a state equivalent to local sleep at the level of the neuro-glia-vascular unit. In particular, a sufficiently strong stimulus can put the model into a state with low both activity and sensitivity to external stimuli. We show that this behavior persists for small ensemble of model units, as well as if we replace the action of neighbors with a positive feedback loop that returns to model unit its own signal with some delay. We conclude that our minimalistic model demonstrates those features that are necessary for further model studies of the spatiotemporal dynamics of sleep.

articleTitle: HTM Spatial Pooler - a Nonparametric Interpretable Feature Selection Algorithm? An Introductory Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Neuroimaging data analysis suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Feature selection plays an important role in mitigating this curse. Here we explore the potential of the Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) Spatial Pooler (SP) as a nonparametric interpretable feature selection algorithm for high-dimensional neuroimaging data. Our results indicate that SP demonstrates comparable performance to other feature selection algorithms in terms of feature stability and classification performance.

articleTitle: Effective dimensionality of neuronal population activity in hippocampus correlates with behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We studied the population activity of hippocampal neurons in mice during novel arena exploration. To quantify the partial synchronization of neuronal activity, we calculated the effective dimensionality of a multidimensional time series of neuronal activity obtained using in vivo using calcium imaging. The effective dimensionality was calculated from the spectra of correlation matrices subjected to the consistent bias correction procedure. Applying this algorithm to mouse neural activity data, we found that the effective activity dimensionality of neuronal populations significantly increased during periods of animal stops. We attribute this finding to the presence of functional ensembles of neurons associated with movements, whose synchronised activity was disrupted during stops.

articleTitle: Two-stage approach based on combination of one-class SVM and CNN for epileptic seizure identification
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Many automated EEG seizure detection methods are able to perform well in terms of precision but fail to keep reasonable recall producing a lot of false positives. To solve this, we propose a two-stage framework combining classical outlier detection methods and neural networks, utilizing real-world EEG data. The first stage uses a one-class support vector machine to filter non-seizure activity, followed by a convolutional neural network to distinguish between false positives and true seizures. Evaluation of metrics tailored for epilepsy detection showed improved precision, with a slight decrease in recall for the proposed approach, suggesting that it may improve the performance of clinical decision support systems.

articleTitle: Detection of Eye Movement Characteristics Using Reservoir Computing in High-Noise Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Accurate real-time detection of saccades is crucial in neuroscience but challenging under high noise levels. We introduce a model based on reservoir computing and tested on simulated eye movement signals with varying $1 / \mathrm{f}$ noise. The model achieved 99.5% accuracy without noise and maintained over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ accuracy even at high noise levels, demonstrating its noise resistance and suitability for real-time brain-computer interfaces.

articleTitle: Brain Connectivity Hypergraphs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Hypergraphs are a rapidly developing area of graph theory that has important applications in many fields, including cognitive neuroscience and medicine. In this paper, we review recent advances in the application of hypergraphs to brain connectivity analysis using brain imaging data. We also present our results on the construction of a hypergraph of brain connectivity during visual perception based on the analysis of magnetoencephalography (MEG) data. The hypergraph approach allowed us to identify individual differences in frequency bands, offering deeper insights into the dynamic nature of brain connectivity. Extending traditional graph theory, we defined a functional network connecting different brain regions (vertices) across time segments by generating edge time series that capture temporal fluctuations in connectivity. Using a coherence measure, we created edge time series to illustrate how connections evolve over time. These series contribute to the edge-to-edge functional connectivity network, highlighting hyperedges as connected components in the absolute value functional connectivity network. We identified key features of the brain network across the delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma frequency bands and examined interactions among the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital lobes in both hemispheres. Our findings support the existence of cortico-cortical interactions, and the resulting hypergraph revealing robust activation patterns in specific brain regions. These results suggest potential integration and multifunctionality within the lobes, providing valuable insights into brain dynamics during visual perception.

articleTitle: Parylene-MoOx nanocomposite memristor crossbar for neuromorphic computing applications
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Memristors, devices demonstrating the resistive switching (RS) effect, have been the subject of active investigation in recent years. It is currently considered that memristors are promising candidates for creating neuromorphic computing systems based on them. In this study, we examined the key characteristics of crossbar array of parylene (PPX)-MoO memristors with a view to subsequent neuromorphic applications. Memristive devices based on PPX$\mathbf{M o O}_{x}$ nanocomposite were found to exhibit cycle-to-cycle (C2C) uniformity and device-to-device (D2D) reproducibility. The coexistence of volatile and non-volatile modes of RS was demonstrated. The first results of a reservoir computing system simulation with PPX-MoO ${ }_{x}$ memristor-based reservoir for the MNIST dataset classification are presented

articleTitle: The development of lifting force in flapping wing robots with variable angle of attack
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Ornithopters, a distinctive class of aircrafts, emulate the wing flapping of birds, bats, and insects. Unlike traditional airplanes, helicopters, and quadcopters, ornithopters generate lift and thrust through the active flapping motion of their wings. This design offers advantages in efficiency, economy, and versatility, while also being significantly quieter than conventional aerial vehicles. Unusual qualities make ornithopters an attractive prospect for different applications, particularly for manned and unmanned aircrafts. Furthermore, this approach has the potential to be integrated with systems that simulate neural circuit activity in the brain, enabling the realization of motor control. This study employed an experimental setup to gather measurements from two models of robotic bird. The results revealed a direct correlation between the wing attack angle and the lift force generated by ornithopters. Specifically, increasing the attack angle resulted in a corresponding increase in lift force in both static and dynamic experiments. The research on ornithopters and motor control of flight holds immense potential for advancing aviation and neurotechnology. Future research avenues could focus on optimizing biomimetic robotic bird design and construction to enhance its efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Network-based approach in fMRI experiment with affective touch
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This research aimed to identify potential differences in resting-state brain networks between the experimental group and healthy individuals. We analyzed 27 experimental subjects (EX) and 11 healthy controls (HC), who all underwent clinical evaluation and functional resting-state Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) testing. We applied network-based measures with the intention of examining functional connectivity network measures across both groups, comparing Rest1 and Rest2 states occurring before and after the experiment, respectively.

articleTitle: Connection between CPG model and servomotor of biomorphic fish robot
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Most animal species locomotion is based on neuronal structures that called central pattern generators (CPG). Locomotor control carried out using such structures has some beneficial features that are useful to apply in robotics. However, the output signal generated by neurons is of a spiking nature, which is suitable for muscle control in animals, but not so suitable for controlling robot servomotors. In this work, we propose a method to connect the neural activity of a spiking neuron CPG model with the propulsion of a biomorphic fishlike robot. The signal transmitted to the robot’s servo is a sinusoid-like curve obtained by converting the muscle contraction variables of our model. Such a signal is well suited for servo control, and at the same time retains such features of CPG as resistance to short-term disturbances in network dynamics and the ability to smoothly modulating.

articleTitle: Intermittent synchronization in a population of neurons with adaptive myelination
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Recently, the myelination process in neuronal circuits was shown to be adaptive, i.e. dependent on the activity of the involved neural cells. We demonstrate that this type of brain plasticity may lead to the emergence of intermittent synchronization, which is the alternation of episodes of synchronous and asynchronous activity in time.

articleTitle: Using artificial neural networks for graffiti detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: To solve the problem of detecting graffiti (tags), an artificial neural network with the YOLOv5 architecture was used. This architecture is known for its high operating speed and low computing power requirements, enabling the quick processing of video streams from a large number of city cameras. To account for the regional characteristics of graffiti, a dataset consisting of 1927 photographs was collected. This dataset is open and available at https://noonv.github.io/KGD/. The accuracy of graffiti detection on the test sample was 0.82.

articleTitle: Memristor structures shape effect: nanoscale resistive switching of dot and lateral electrochemical titanium oxide
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper presents the results of the formation of lateral $(2000 \times 2000 \mathrm{~nm})$ and dot $(50 \mathrm{~nm})$ nanostructures of electrochemical titanium oxide, as well as the results of studying their resistive switching. It was shown that the resulting structures exhibit a resistive switching effect. An endurance test was carried out for 100 switching cycles and a retention test for 450 seconds.

articleTitle: Synaptic plasticity in the nanocrystalline ZnO cross-point for neuromorphic systems of AI
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work shows the results of multilevel resistive switching, as well as synaptic plasticity of neuron-like memristive cross-point based on nanocrystalline zinc oxide films. It has been shown that when the amplitude and duration of the input pulse are varied, the crosspoint exhibits 6 resistive states and switching energy in a few pJ. Also, the cross-point exhibit paired-pulse facilitation and depression at pulse interval from 1 ms to 10 ms and from 50 ms to 100 ms, respectively. The obtained results can be used for hardware implementation of neural networks, neuromorphic structures of robotic complexes, prostheses, and artificial intelligence systems.

articleTitle: Collective Dynamics in a Network of Electronic FitzHugh-Nagumo Generators Coupled via a Hub
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We experimentally study the collective dynamics of analog electronic FitzHugh-Nagumo generators in a multilayer network. A three-layer network is considered, the two outer layers of which are rings of bidirectionally coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo generators, and one inner layer is a hub in the form of a FitzHugh-Nagumo generator, which provides bidirectional coupling between the two rings. It is shown that with repulsive couplings of FitzHugh-Nagumo generators inside the rings and repulsive interlayer couplings, frequency synchronization of all network generators occurs.

articleTitle: Intermittent behavior near the boundary of generalized synchronization in systems with different topologies of attractors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This report contains a brief review of recent achievements of the author team in the field of the research of intermittent generalized synchronization in systems with different topologies of attractors. The cases of interaction of unidirectionally and mutually coupled chaotic dynamical systems with simple and complex topologies of attractors and methods for the analysis of such systems are considered. The presence of multistability in the intermittent generalized synchronization regime has also been discussed.

articleTitle: Dynamics of reward-based training of piece-wise linear recurrent neural networks for context-dependent decision making
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work, we consider an ensemble of recurrent neural networks which are reinforcement-trained for the cognitive-like task of context-dependent perceptual decision making. The systems are characterized by the actor-critic architecture and consist of piece-wise linear neurons in the form of rectified linear units. We study dynamic mechanisms underlying the task completing during trial implementation as well as the dynamics of training, i.e., the process of how particular dynamical and structural aspects emerge in the course of reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: Real-Time Identification of Dynamic Process Characteristics in Complex Technical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced technology for modifying and strengthening geometrically complex surfaces of engineering products using a next-generation plasma torch. The process is optimized through a two-stage control system that manages complex dynamic processes. The control system incorporates feedback channels to monitor the effects of low-temperature plasma on the product’s surface, utilizing parameters from both electrical and optical signals to ensure precise and effective modification.

articleTitle: Reservoir computing shows partial statistical dynamics prediction of two coupled stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We train a reservoir computing-based echo state network to predict the stochastic dynamics of two coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons excited by external Gaussian noise. We describe the design principles of the echo state network and the coupled oscillator network. Results show that prediction quality of the dynamics of each neuron varies despite their high coupling strength.

articleTitle: Neural Processing of Social Stimuli in High vs. Low Social Anxiety Individuals: A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Social anxiety is characterized by fear in various socially related situations. Research demonstrates that people with high social anxiety have lower self-esteem and experience negative impacts from this state. The current pilot study aimed to investigate neural responses to social stimuli in individuals with high and low social anxiety. Fifty-seven participants completed an online screening form to assess anxiety levels, with four participants selected for each group based on their scores (High Social Anxiety group: M_age = 20.57, SD = 4.27; Low Social Anxiety group: M_age $=\mathbf{2 8. 5}, \mathbf{S D}=\mathbf{7. 1 8}$). Participants underwent EEG recordings while being exposed to facial expression stimuli. Results revealed lower event-related potentials (ERPs) in individuals with high social anxiety compared to those with low social anxiety. These findings suggest altered neural processing of social cues in individuals with high social anxiety, highlighting the need for further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

articleTitle: Learning Foreign Languages by Adults Using Immersive Virtual Reality Systems: Review of Recent Studies (2014-2024)
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the accelerating dynamics of the modern world, many people refuse traditional methods of foreign language learning in the classroom in favor of modern digital technologies, such as immersive virtual reality (iVR). iVR produces a multisensory flow, which makes learning process more efficient, interesting and faster. However, the long-term effect of application iVR technology to foreign language learning is still not well investigated. In this work, we conducted a literature search on the presence of a formative experiment aimed at acquiring a second language in iVR by adults without clinical complications. Data extraction was carried out from Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed databases according to a query “((VIRTUAL REALITY) OR (IMMERSIVE REALITY)) AND (LANGUAGE AND LEARNING)) AND PUBYEAR>2014”. As a result, from the 783 scientific sources 18 experimental works were selected (2,3%). These experimental works were classified on the orientation of the iVR simulator into language skills, listening skills, memorizing words, and social interaction. Of the 18 experimental studies, 10 showed a positive effect from the use of iVR in learning a foreign language, the remaining 8 studies did not contain estimates of the effect.

articleTitle: Memory Block Development for Neuromorph Setup: experimental study
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this study, we experimentally realized and tested a “Memory” block based on a network of four chemical oscillators connected in a circular arrangement with inhibitory pulse couplings, regulated by Hebb’s rules. Here, memory is conceptualized as the transition between internal dynamic modes of the network in response to external signals. We observed the switching from one stable network mode, AP (antiphase), to another, WR (walk reverse), facilitated by the management of auxiliary cells responsible for regulating connection strength. This “Memory” block will be utilized in future neuromorphic devices.

articleTitle: Comparison of non-stationarity heart rate variability in healthy volunteers and patients with impaired autonomic control of blood circulation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The method of analyzing heart rate variability is used to study the work of autonomic control of blood circulation. Changes in heart rate variability may indicate pathologies of autonomic control of blood circulation. We used methods to analyze heart rate non-stationarity. The goal of our work to study the possibility of analyzing the non-stationarity of heart rate variability to screen the type of dysfunction of the autonomic control of blood circulation. We analyzed four groups of subjects: healthy volunteers, patients with arterial hypertension, patients with chronic heart failure and patients with denervated hearts. We analyzed the sequence of RR-intervals and calculated four indices the non-stationarity of heart rate variability for each subject: standard deviation of the sequence of RR-intervals; time until the first zero value of the autocorrelation coefficient of the sequence of RR-intervals; the criterion for the difference between one-dimensional distributions of a sequence of RR-intervals; Euclidean distance between vectors of coefficients of the regression equation the sequences of RR-intervals. We obtained results indicating that the compared methods of analyzing non-stationarity demonstrate correlated results and complement each other, providing different information about the baroreflex control of heart rhythm.

articleTitle: Experimental Realization of Neuron-Like Activity Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: For the experimental implementation of neurallike systems, we apply an approach based on representing a system of differential equations describing a self-oscillating system in the form of a set of coupled first-order RC-filters. Using this approach, an electronic circuit of a Hindmarsh-Rose neuron is proposed.

articleTitle: Cascade CNN-based model for epileptic seizure diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Automated seizure detection is a complex task in epilepsy diagnosis, mainly due to the rarity of seizures. Automatic solutions often lead to a high number of false positives. This study proposes a two-stage approach that combines iterative refinement algorithms and convolutional neural networks to minimize false positives in seizure detection task. The method was tested on a real-world EEG dataset using epilepsy-specific metrics and demonstrated a significant reduction in false positives, demonstrating the potential of the method for use in clinical decision-support systems.

articleTitle: Working memory capacity in spiking neural network with two types of plasticity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Working memory (WM) is a brain system for short-term storage and manipulation of information and plays an important role in complex cognitive tasks. Most WM models contain pre-formed content-specific structures of neurons for loading specific objects into memory, without considering the flexibility of WM. We develop on previous research and propose a flexible model of WM based on synaptic theory considering two types of plasticity: Tsodyks-Markram plasticity and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP). The synaptic theory of WM hypothesizes that items are stored silently by temporally potentiated synapses in a distinct neuronal population. We show that external stimulation can form such populations due to the mechanisms of STDP. The capacity of the WM model with two types of plasticity was studied in dependence of synaptic time scales and learning rate. It is shown that estimated WM capacity of model with two types of plasticity depends on intrinsic neural and synaptic parameters and could be scaled by STDP parameters.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Linear and Exact Control Laws in Zonotope-Based MPC
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Zonotopes are a special type of symmetric polytopes that have been an emerging control design tool, being used for such tasks as state estimation and explicit model predictive control. Zonotopes are used to represent sets of control actions and states, encountered by trajectories of the system, originating from a set of initial conditions. However, an inherent limitation of zonotope geometry (their symmetries, for example) limits the range of control design scenarios where zonotopes can be used as an adequate set representation, while the use of linear control laws can prevent change in the desired behavior of the closed-loop system. The first issue can be remedied by the use of constrained zonotopes, which can represent arbitrary polytopes. In this paper we present an analysis of the second problem, demonstrating the effects of linear control law and exact, convex programmingbased control law. We demonstrate the efficacy of the use of the lifting-up method for constrained zonotopes as pertains to control design.

articleTitle: Extreme events in epilepsy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, we aim to provide a brief review of the research of epileptic extreme events. The main topics of interest include extreme value theory approaches used to describe mechanisms in the epileptic brain and to detect/predict seizures as well as possible applications of the results obtained in medical diagnostics. The main purpose of the review is to draw attention to this relevant area of research.

articleTitle: Novel memristive STDP approach and neural clusters formation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is the most common mechanism of long-term synaptic plasticity and the main approach for neural networks learning. The traditional memristive community is dominated by the approach in which the memristor changes its conductance (and thus its coupling weight) due to the action of neuron signals applied directly to the memristor contacts. We propose a system for controlling the state of the memristor, in which the spikes of pre- and postsynaptic neurons do not change the state of the memristor due to their small amplitude but trigger an additional block that affects the memristor. We studied the proposed novel STDP approach in numerical simulation with second order memristor model. The magnitude of change in the memristor state parameter turns out to be very similar to the classical STDP rules of synaptic plasticity We showed the possibility of cluster formation in spiking neural network by memristive STDP under external stimulation.

articleTitle: Effect of Blockade of the 5-HT4 Receptors on the Calcium Activity of Neuron-Glial Networks in vitro
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: recent data suggests that the serotonergic system is an important regulator of neuroplasticity and is involved in the organization of functional neural networks. We have researched the effect of blockade of the serotonin receptor type 4 on the parameters of intercellular calcium signal transmission in neuron-glial networks in primary hippocampal cell cultures. Our results demonstrate that in vitro blockade of 5-HT4 receptors leads to disruption of intercellular calcium signaling and destruction of functional connections between cells in the network.

articleTitle: Possibilities of rehabilitation using virtual reality technologies in patients with post-stroke cognitive impairment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This work tests the effectiveness of rehabilitation of patients after ischaemic stroke using partially immersive virtual reality technologies.

articleTitle: Memristive Artificial Neural Networks Accuracy Evaluation Using Data-Driven Models
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Memristive devices are promising candidates for the role of analog synapses in the hardware implementation of energy-efficient artificial neural networks (ANNs). However, variations in the resistance of memristive devices lead to errors in the values of the weighting coefficients of neuron synapses and, accordingly, can have a negative impact on the accuracy of the functioning of ANNs based on them. This paper proposes an approach to creating models of memristive devices that can be used to assess the impact of their variations on the quality of ANN functioning. The implementation of this approach is demonstrated using the example of an ANN trained to solve a image classification problem.

articleTitle: Indicators of functional outcome of patients with different degrees of cognitive deficit in the acute period of ischemic stroke
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study analyses medical indicators that influence the adverse outcome of rehabilitation of patients after ischaemic stroke with varying degrees of cognitive impairment.

articleTitle: Simple model of neurogliovascular unit activity with noradrenaline leading force
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work we present a model of a neuroglivascular unit associated with a neuronal ensemble. We combine calcium dynamics in the astrocyte, the cascade of synthesis of arachidonic acid and its derivatives, as well as the activity of the network of inhibitory and excitatory neurons with changes in local blood flow. We add equations to the model for extracellular neurotransmitters such as GABA, glutamate, and norepinephrine. We show that the resulting model can exhibit different types of behavior, and also shows a significant connection between the functioning of the neural network and its supporting components.

articleTitle: Identification of Mechanisms and Biomarkers of Learning Efficiency Based on Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving world, the ability to efficiently learn and process new information is increasingly crucial. This study aims to identify mechanisms and biomarkers of learning efficiency using multimodal data. We designed and conducted a neurophysiological experiment simulating educational activities over two days with 26 participants aged 18 to 30. Behavioral data such as memory time-the interval from stimulus presentation to participant response-were analyzed to understand cognitive processes during learning. Participants underwent the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20) test to assess their psychophysiological state before and after the experiment. Our findings reveal a statistically significant decrease in performance $50-60$ minutes after presenting new information, aligning with Ebbinghaus’s forgetting curve. This suggests that unfamiliar information not properly assimilated within this time frame does not enter long-term memory. The results underscore the importance of reviewing new information shortly after learning to enhance retention. By identifying key behavioral markers and understanding their impact on learning efficiency, this study contributes to the development of intelligent expert systems that optimize educational activities based on individual psychophysiological characteristics.

articleTitle: Differences in optimal community structure in brain connectivity organization in major depressive disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We analyzed fMRI data from healthy control subjects (94 subjects) and patients with major depressive episode (70 patients). The preprocessed activity signals extracted with statistical parametric mapping from fMRI were divided into parcellations according to the anatomical labeling atlas. Our findings indicate that patients with major depressive disorder exhibit network organization that is both less locally specialized and less globally integrated. Specifically, our research reveals differences in network segregation rather than integration in patients. The discrepancies between our results and previous studies may be attributed to differences in methodology, depression diversity, sample sizes, and co-occurring factors such as stress and anxiety.

articleTitle: The Relationship Between IQ Level and Functional Brain Network Centrality During Cognitive Activity in Children
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the current study, we restored the functional brain networks of children aged 10 to 12 years old when performing cognitive tasks related to learning processes. To calculate connectivity, we chose the method of calculating the imaginary part of coherence (ICOH) in the theta, alpha and beta frequency ranges. To characterize each network, we calculated the main network indicators for them - the average degree of conditionality, the clustering coefficient, efficiency and average centrality. As a result of the search for correlates of network metrics and data on the performance of the tasks of the subjects, we found the presence of positive correlations of network centrality in the alpha frequency range with both the effectiveness of complex cognitive tasks and the overall level of intelligence of the subjects. Thus, the greater integration of the functional network contributes to a more efficient operation of complex cognitive functions.

articleTitle: Modeling of systems that imitate biologically similar movements of a fish robot and a snake robot
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The use of central rhythm generators (CPGs) as control systems has recently received more and more attention. Such systems allow us to solve the problem of path prediction. They have higher stability. However, there are a number of problems in designing successful and working systems such as a real robot -CPG. For example, it is necessary to synchronize the operating time of the CPG model and the actuator. There are also difficulties with using CPG on different robots. Even when modeling robots with similar prototypes: fish, salamanders, snakes, it is necessary not only to change the number of segments of the control system to control the actuators, but also to completely change the operating parameters of the CPG for proper interaction with the environment. Next, we demonstrate a CPG capable of controlling a virtual robot fish and a ground robot snake. The model is capable of moving forward and turning left and right. It is possible to connect external sensors to transmit information about an obstacle to the system and perform a turn under its influence.

articleTitle: Determination of the psychological and pedagogical substantiation of the cognitive functions influence on the development of higher education students’ universal competencies
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: the article analyzes the role of the competency-based approach in higher education, with a particular focus on universal competencies and their significance in shaping a well-rounded student personality. It provides a terminological clarification and examines the impact of cognitive ability development on the formation of students’ universal competencies.

articleTitle: Investigation of Time-Frequency Characteristics of Nighttime EEG Signals in Various Brain Regions Depending on Chronotype
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper reports the results of a partial-time analysis of EEG signals from healthy volunteers obtained during the recording of polysomnography with an expanded arrangement of electrodes (19 leads). An analysis of the characteristics of frequency patterns (their number, duration, and energy power) was carried out in 20 frequency ranges (from 1 to 40 Hz) in 5 areas of the brain (central, occipital, frontal, left, and right hemispheres). A comparison of the obtained characteristics was carried out according to the chronotypes of the respondents (“rhythmic” and “arrhythmic"). Based on the results of the study, it was possible to demonstrate chronobiological patterns of nocturnal EEG activity in healthy volunteers.

articleTitle: Default resting state EEG activity mathematical analysis as the new neurophysiological technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The relative stagnation of the EEG method significantly complicates the assessment of clinical borderline psychopathological states that are actively observed in modern society. The purpose of the study was to show the possibilities of mathematical analysis of EEG microstates as a new method of clinical EEG diagnostics. The results made it possible to determine that the use of mathematical processing of EEG signals makes it possible to visualize individual cognitive profiles of the disease, which differ significantly from indicators of normal brain activity. These studies make it possible to offer practical psychiatry a new objective method for studying human cognitive functions.

articleTitle: Preprocessing of the Initial Data with Discrete Wavelet Transform to Predict Time Series Using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this study, we attempted to increase the prediction accuracy of the long short-term memory (LSTM) model by preprocessing of the initial time series data with discrete wavelet transform (DWT). The methane concentration time series was decomposed into one approximating and three detailing components with DWT. These four components along with temperature time series were used to train LSTM models. Two predictive models were trained on the preprocessed data (LSTM&DWT (temperature) and LSTM&DWT (time) models), while two other predictive models were trained on an untransformed data (LSTM (temperature) and LSTM (time) models). The prediction was calculated as the sum of the predictions for each component. In general, the proposed LSTM&DWT (temperature) and LSTM&DWT (time) models outperformed LSTM (temperature) and LSTM (time) models. The LSTM&DWT (temperature) model was the most accurate at all assessed performance indices, which was also marked in the Taylor diagram. The result was than proved by the 48 -hour prediction of CH<inf>4</inf> concentrations built with four LSTM-based models.

articleTitle: Comparison of Methods for Modeling Phase Dynamics Using the Models of Different Orders
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Analyzing the intensity and directionality of couplings between different systems is a very complex and important task in studying the functioning of physiological systems. To carry out such a study, the phase dynamics modeling method can be used. We propose to simplify the structure of the phase dynamics model in order to reduce time for calculating estimates of coupling intensity. It is shown that the proposed changes made it possible to reduce the time for calculating the coupling estimates by 2.97 times, while coupling intensity obtained by the two methods differ by less than 1 percent. The changes in the phase dynamics modeling method proposed in this paper will make it easier to work with long time series.

articleTitle: Distance and relative speed estimation of vehicles moving in the same direction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Intelligent vehicle systems often use expensive hardware to calculate distances and speeds of surrounding objects. This paper presents two algorithms for estimating the relative speed of vehicles using monocular cameras. The first algorithm relies on license plate detection with a known size, while a modified version incorporates car dimension calculations. The second algorithm utilizes pre-calibrated cameras based on marked driveways. An experiment was conducted to compare the efficiency of the algorithms. Experiments showed that the most accurate results for estimation the distance to vehicles were obtained by the preliminary marking method with an error close to 0%. However, this method has significant limitations, such as camera fixation and stabilization requirements. The second most accurate method, based on using vehicle width values, demonstrated an error range of 1.5% to 3.3%. Unlike the first method, this algorithm does not require strict camera fixation and stabilization.

articleTitle: Development of methods for studying the synchronization of circuits in autonomic regulation of blood circulation based on the analysis of the statistical properties of instantaneous phase differences
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The statistical properties of the distributions of instantaneous phase differences of low-frequency oscillations in the circuits of autonomic regulation of blood circulation were studied by analyzing the signals of RR-intervals and photoplethysmograms of healthy volunteers and patients with myocardial infarction and arterial hypertension. During the analysis of experimental data, a comparison of four quantitative indices for assessing the statistical properties of the distributions of instantaneous phase differences was conducted. Based on the obtained results, a conclusion was drawn regarding the feasibility of using the proposed quantitative indices for diagnosing diseases of the circulatory system.

articleTitle: Investigating the spinal cord CPG neural circuits with emphasis on STDP mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In our current position paper, we present a novel approach for the neurostimulation of self-learning CPG using feedback loops and STDP-based circuitry. The scale-up of the previously presented work to the scale of the complete spinal circuitry with inputs from the brainstem and outputs to the motor neuronal pools - muscles feedback loops.

articleTitle: Non-stationarity of the natural frequency of the sympathetic control loop of the heart rhythm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In recent years, heart rate variability biofeedback has rapidly developed and is used to improve the condition and treat a number of diseases in clinical practice. However, despite this, assessing the person’s resonance frequency still remains a complex task, entailing many still unanswered questions. In this work, we investigated the stationarity of the resonance frequency in repeated experiments for young healthy volunteers, as well as the possibility of using rhythmic skeletal muscle tension of the arms and legs instead of the complex requirement of breathing at unusually slow frequencies. The experimental sample consisted of 7 volunteers, for whom a series of 5 experiments were conducted (4 recordings with slow breathing, 1 recording with rhythmic skeletal muscle tension). There were recorded ECG and respiratory signals. During the data analysis, we constructed resonance curves and determined resonance frequency values. It was found that the resonance frequency is not stationary for a particular person. Rhythmic skeletal muscle tension of the arms and legs can be an alternative to breathing at slow frequencies.

articleTitle: Circadian rhythms in the interaction between the processes of autonomic control of blood circulation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Circadian rhythms are important for the regulation of the cardiovascular system and can serve as a therapeutic target for improving existing and developing new treatments for circulatory diseases. We monitored blood pressure, heart rate, amplitude of low-frequency oscillations of the sequence of RR-interval and the total percentage of phase synchronization between the low-frequency processes of autonomic control of heart rate and mean arterial pressure in 17 young healthy volunteers for 24 hours. The results of our studies indicate slow-frequency oscillations with a period of about 2.8 hours in controlled processes and their correlation with circadian fluctuations in blood pressure and heart rate.

articleTitle: How internal noise impacts simplified deep neural network during training
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, we analyse the impact of additive and multiplicative uncorrelated white Gaussian noise on a simplified deep neural network during training. For this purpose, we train artificial neural network to recognize the set of handwritten digits (MNIST database). The network consists of three layers (one input, output and hidden layer), where hidden layer has 20 neurons with sigmoid activation function. The internal noise in artificial neural networks can arise in the case of analog (hardware) neural networks, which artificial neurons and their connectivity are based on physical principles. Therefore, it is of particular interest to study how internal noise impacts the final performance. Here we introduce the noise into the neurons of hidden layer. We show, that for some cases additive and multiplicative noise can increase the training speed.

articleTitle: Recursive map neuron model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Study of spiking neural networks is a promising scientific direction of modern interdisciplinary research. Spiking networks have demonstrated high efficacy in processing and classification tasks on various datasets (pictures, acoustic signals, biological signals) and in robotics (navigation, movement control, interaction with media etc.) One of the main problems of this type of neural networks is high computational and implementational cost. This problem rises from computational complexity of many nonlinearities in neuronal models and nonlinear synaptic functions. Novel low-computational-cost models of spiking neurons and synapses could be a possible decision of this problem. Here, we propose a new discrete recursive neuron model. The model demonstrates rich spiking and bursting dynamic repertoire and requires relatively small computational resources. Moreover, the proposed model could be implemented by standard discrete logic elements.

articleTitle: Comparison of Wearable Video-based Eye Tracking and EOG for Oculomotor Activity Detection in Specific Research Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Oculomotor activity measurement is crucial for understanding visual perception and cognitive processes in neuroscience. This study conducts a comparative analysis of wearable video-based eye tracking (Pupil Core) and electrooculography (EOG) in detecting eye movements during a neurophysiological task based on Raven’s Advanced Progressive Matrices (APM). Fourteen calibration sessions were performed using five calibration points, and data synchronization was achieved through the Lab Streaming Layer protocol. Both eye tracking methods were calibrated using optimal affine transformation matrices to minimize discrepancies between fixation points and calibration markers. The calibration error averaged 66.4 pixels for the Pupil Core system and 64.73 pixels for EOG data, indicating comparable accuracy between the two methods. Despite EOG’s susceptibility to artifacts from muscle contractions and wire movements, its performance suggests it is a viable alternative to video-based systems, particularly in environments with challenging lighting conditions or when long-term monitoring is required.

articleTitle: Implementation of Decision Tree Models in Differentiating Hard-to-Diagnose Lung Nodules
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We have studied the importance of various lung characteristics obtained through computed tomography (CT), in conjunction with other factors, for distinguishing between lung pathologies such as hamartoma (HM) and tuber-culoma (TB). We have developed a model based on the decision tree algorithm trained on clinical data. This enabled us to identify key characteristics and their interactions, as well as to define the main clinical factors that precisely characterize HM and TB states. The model demonstrated that the radiology factor characterizing changes in the surrounding tissue of the pathological nodule has the most contribution.

articleTitle: Recovery of hidden macroscopic signals in a Kuramoto phase oscillators network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We are solving the task of recovering the hidden signals in a model network. As a model we choose Kuramoto phase oscillator with adaptation of couplings. We divide the network for six parts and calculate macroscopic signals. We propose that knowing only a part of macroscopic signals allows us to recover the rest unknown ones. We show that using Reservoir computing successfully solves the problem.

articleTitle: Single Spiking Neuron Learns Dynamic Stimuli
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper we show that simple spiking neural network is able to learn dynamic stimuli by memorizing specific patterns and ignoring others without implementing any recurrent connections. The proposed model consists of one spiking neuron with trainable synaptic connections from neuron-like asynchronous signals. The model was trained in biologically plausible fashion, utilizing exact timings when spikes occur. We expect that future research on investigation of the ability of network stabilization while learning different patterns will lead to processing of complex patterns.

articleTitle: Biomarkers of coronary heart disease based on the analysis of the form of the ST segment of the electrocardiogram
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Coronary heart disease is one of the primary causes of death worldwide. An open question is development of quantitative indexes - biomarkers, used for the detection of the disease in the early stages in home cardiographs. In the work proposed two quantitative indexes, characterizing the shape Twave of the electrocardiogram. Proposed indexes were tested in the analysis of healthy volunteers and patients with newly diagnosed coronary heart disease. The joint use of the proposed indexes demonstrated the possibility of diagnosing patients with sensitivity of 1.00, specificity of 0.78, F-score of 0.87.

articleTitle: Robot navigation under uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Robot navigation is a popular sphere in modern science. Uncertainty can arise due to various factors, such as environmental change, inaccuracy of sensors measurements, the presence of obstacles. The paper discusses the types of navigation systems, methods for searching for a fragment on a map. The experiments carried out showed the effectiveness of the methods depending on the size of the desired fragment and map for correlation, brute force and Fourier-based methods.

articleTitle: Recognizing patterns in images using a small spiking neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We study a spiking neural network consisting of a small number of LIF neurons, capable of recognizing horizontal and vertical patterns in a 3*3 pixel image. Neural learning is carried out using the STDP algorithm. The network is trained and tested on a sample of ${6 0 0 0}$ images. It is shown that the investigated neural network has an accuracy of ${9 9 \%}$ on the training set and ${9 7 \%}$ on the test set.

articleTitle: Spatial model of neurogliovascular unit: arachidonic acid can control the stability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Arachidonic acid metabolites can have both vasoconstrictor and vasodilator effects, thereby influencing neuronal activity. In this work, to analyze possible patterns of activity of nervous tissue in response to changes in the metabolic profile, a mathematical model of a spatially distributed system of connected neurogliovascular units was developed. We simulate the influence of arachidonic acid metabolites on the dynamics of the neurogliovascular unit during cortical spreading depression in order to determine the ways in which astrocytic activity influences the spatiotemporal characteristics of the propagating cortical depression wave. It is assumed that in the future the results of the theoretical study can be used to find ways to remove nervous tissue from pathological conditions that occur in epilepsy, migraines and a number of neurodegenerative diseases, including those associated with the occurrence of cortical depression waves.

articleTitle: Functional Brain Network Analysis in Children Performing Working Memory Tasks: EEG Study
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the current study, we analyzed EEG data from children 10-12 years old during the performance of Working Memory Task. To calculate connectivity between some areas of brain (Frontal, Left and Right Temporal, Central and Occipital-Parietal) we calculated average Phase-Locking Value between each areas. We find relationships between reaction time and Left Temporal - Central and Right Temporal - Central synchronizations. These results can indicate a relationship between the speed of decoding information during working memory load and the phase synchronizations between mentioned brain areas.

articleTitle: Using Brainwave Entropy to Evaluate Visual Search Performance in School-Aged Children
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper analyzes data from a neurophysiological experiment based on a visual search task. The study investigates methods for predicting response time based on the entropy of the energies of key brain rhythms, such as theta, alpha, and beta, in different brain regions. The aim is to develop methods for predicting task performance efficiency using neurophysiological parameters.

articleTitle: Behavioral Enhancement of Associative Learning Requires Overlapping Neuronal Populations
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: A weak memory can be converted into a long-term form if it is preceded by another weak training episode or exploration of a new environment. Current hypotheses explain the mechanisms behind this phenomenon, suggesting that the formation of new memories involves a population of neurons that are pre-activated by previous cognitive experiences. We visualized neuronal activity from two distinct cognitive episodes separated in time using transgenic Arc-Cre-Tomato mice. Mice were trained using a weak cued fear conditioning protocol that typically does not lead to long-term memory formation. However, when re-trained with the same cue, significant memory improvement was observed. In contrast, different cues did not produce this effect. Our analysis revealed a higher percentage of overlapping neuronal populations in the prelimbic cortex, primary auditory cortex, and amygdala in mice trained with the same cue. These findings suggest that cumulative learning and memory potentiation depend on the involvement of overlapping neuronal populations and only occur when these events engage the same groups of brain neurons.

articleTitle: SPSA-based Consensus Algorithm for Collaborative Learning with Heavy-Tailed Noises
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Collaborative learning is a fast growing branch of machine learning. This approach allows to learn a global model keeping user data private and to easily scale a system. However, many algorithms for collaborative learning rely on aggregation of parameters learned by an each individual agent on a single server followed by a global model obtaining. With such approach the server becomes a single failure point. Another common assumption concerns noises in data. Most of the works consider only noises with finite variance. Altough it is known, that heavy-tailed noises arise in many real models.

articleTitle: Biomarkers of Early Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper reviews the correlation between cognitive failure after ischaemic stroke and the following independent variables: clinical diagnostic scale scores, evoked potentials and CXC family chemokines, in order to establish the influence of these parameters on patients’ cognitive recovery.

articleTitle: Hardware electronic circuit modeling neuron with diode based non-linearity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is hardware implementation of the nonlinear electronic generator of neuron-like activity developed previously using nGSPICE software. Based on the previously developed circuits, we simplified the design by reducing the number of components and rearranging nonlinear elements. Various approximations of the nonlinear function were considered by means of different number n of diodes in the circuit, and the dependence of the output signal on n was investigated. Quasi-linear and nonlinear generation regimes were studied. Also, a simple partial bifurcation analysis was performed in order to study the mechanisms of oscillation birth in the circuit. As a result, taking into account the non-ideality of physical components, we came to the conclusion that our circuit developed previously in the ngSPICE simulator can be easily constructed in the hardware.

articleTitle: Reconstructing the model equation for the autonomic control of the mean arterial pressure from rat data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Several parameters of the autonomic control of the mean arterial pressure, namely the time delay in the feedback loop, parameters of the nonlinear transfer function between the arterial pressure and baroreceptor activity, and inertial properties of the system, cannot be measured directly. Therefore, the ability to evaluate them indirectly and reconstruct an personalized mathematical model of the autonomic control is valuable for both fundamental investigation and diagnostics of the cardiovascular system. We developed an algorithm that tackles this problem. We initially tested the algorithm on the data, generated by a mathematical model of the autonomic control of the mean arterial pressure with added noises of various nature, and the algorithm demonstrated sufficient resistance to noise. Then we tested the algorithm against the experimental rat data. The time series from the reconstructed model closely resembled the experimental data in terms of spectral properties and the shape of oscillations, and estimations of the parameters were stable across the record. Due to that stability, we can assume that the reconstructed values represent the intrinsic characteristics of the system.

articleTitle: About the possibility of using generative neural networks for malicious «high-quality»-purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 8th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The publication is devoted to examine the capabilities of modern neural networks based on large language models for creating malicious «high-quality»programs.
